title: BOS-713 — a dropped --host ssh tunnel shows a named reconnecting screen that keeps [q]uit available and recovers to the session board unaided

scenes.title: The tunnel drop names the ssh destination it is redialling and keeps the user's escape hatch on screen

waitFor.label: the wait screen names the exact ssh destination boss is redialling, so a user driving several hosts knows which one dropped

steps.caption: The forwarded socket stopped answering; boss shows the reconnecting screen instead of exiting with a dial error.

expect.text: Boss keeps redialling and resumes automatically
expect.label: the screen promises unaided recovery — the user is told to wait, not to restart boss
the polling footer confirms the screen is actively probing, not frozen
the retained action bar keeps a way out, so an indefinite wait never strands the user
the escalation path is a copy-able command against the same destination, for a tunnel that does not come back

steps.caption: Destination, the automatic-retry promise, the escape hatch, and the manual check are all on one frame.

scenes.title: When the tunnel answers again the TUI proceeds to the remote daemon's session board with no keystroke

waitFor.label: the session board replaces the wait screen on its own — recovery needs no input from the user

steps.caption: The redial succeeded; boss resumes startup against the recovered tunnel rather than making the user relaunch.
The wait screen releases the alt-screen and Home completes its first session refresh against the recovered client.

expect.label: a real session row from the daemon renders, so the recovered client is genuinely serving data
a second seeded row confirms the whole board came back, not a single lucky cell

steps.caption: The board is fully populated: the reconnecting screen handed over to a working client.
